items.title: CFTC sues New Mexico over prediction-market preemption (8th state)
items.facts: On 2026-06-12 the CFTC filed suit in federal court against the State of New Mexico, seeking a declaratory judgment that federal law grants it exclusive authority over event contracts and a permanent injunction barring the state from enforcing preempted gaming laws against CFTC registrants. The action follows New Mexico's state-court suit against CFTC-registrant KalshiEX LLC alleging its prediction-market offerings are unlawful online sports betting. The release states New Mexico joins AZ, CT, IL, NY, MN, RI, and WI.

items.title: Nevada gaming regulator seeks to hold Kalshi in contempt over prediction-market geofencing
items.facts: As reported by the Las Vegas Review-Journal (and corroborated by InterGame and Gambling Insider), on 2026-06-12 the Nevada Gaming Control Board petitioned the First Judicial District Court in Carson City to find KalshiEx LLC in contempt for allegedly not complying with a May 18 order requiring it to geofence its website so it cannot offer sports-, election-, or entertainment-related event contracts to anyone located in Nevada. The Board asked the court to impose sanctions, including disgorgement of profits from Nevada transactions or daily penalties until compliance. A Kalshi spokesperson said the company has complied, attributed the issue to a technology glitch, and called the filing a 'PR stunt.'
items.source_label: Las Vegas Review-Journal (reporting the Nevada GCB court filing)

items.issuing_body: Coalition for Fair Markets (NADEX, Kalshi, Polymarket/QCX)
items.title: Prediction-market coalition sues Kentucky over 14.25% tax on event-contract trading
items.facts: As reported by SBC Americas (first reported by the Associated Press and corroborated by Gambling Insider), on 2026-06-12 the Coalition for Fair Markets — comprising Crypto.com's North American Derivatives Exchange (NADEX), Kalshi, and Polymarket's U.S. exchange QCX — filed suit in Franklin Circuit Court to block Kentucky from implementing a 14.25% tax on prediction-market transaction fees set to take effect Jan. 1, 2027, arguing the measure unlawfully targets federally regulated event-contract exchanges and is preempted by federal derivatives law. The enacted package (HB 757 and HB 904) also bars state-licensed gaming operators from doing business with platforms offering sports event-contract trading in Kentucky, a prohibition due to take effect next month. Kentucky Attorney General Russell Coleman, a named defendant, said his office 'will defend these statutes.'
items.source_label: SBC Americas (reporting the Coalition for Fair Markets filing; first reported by the Associated Press)
